# Clark Huang

> Public learning pages on AI-native software workflows: short video lessons (AI Tips, Software Engineering 101 and 201) and a preview of Silicon Valley C Players, a free OpenBook.

The HTML pages are for people. Every page also has an `index.md` twin and an `AGENTS.md` that an AI tool can fetch directly, so you can summarize the material and navigate the site from a single link, without using a browser.

Optional: start with [https://clarkhuang.github.io/AGENTS.md](https://clarkhuang.github.io/AGENTS.md) for how to help a reader, then come back here for the catalog.

## Site

- [Home](https://clarkhuang.github.io/index.md): about Clark Huang and the series on this site
- [AGENTS.md](https://clarkhuang.github.io/AGENTS.md): how to navigate and what not to invent
- [llms-full.txt](https://clarkhuang.github.io/llms-full.txt): fuller text of the book preview, cover description, and lesson catalog
- [lessons.json](https://clarkhuang.github.io/lessons.json): machine-readable catalog of every lesson, with rules, video URLs, and durations
- [book.json](https://clarkhuang.github.io/book.json): OpenBook preview catalog, including cover description, transcripts, captions and chapters
- [REBUILD.md](https://clarkhuang.github.io/REBUILD.md): how to rebuild production and staging

## AI Tips

- [Series index](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/index.md): Short lessons on working with AI in everyday work: how these tools actually behave, the habits that catch mistakes early, and how to get more reliable results.

- [Lesson 1: Paste First, Ask Second](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/01-paste-first-ask-second/index.md): When an AI gives you a useless answer, it is usually not the AI's fault: you described the problem instead of showing it. Without the real material, it can only guess. Paste the screenshot, document, error message,…
- [Lesson 2: Ask for Proof, Not “Done”](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/02-ask-for-proof/index.md): When a bot says “done”, it is usually reporting the status of the step it ran, not whether the outcome you wanted is true. Five short examples show the gap, and none of them is a bot misbehaving. The fix is to ask…
- [Lesson 3: Define the Number Before You Ask for It](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/03-define-the-number-before-you-ask-for-it/index.md): Ask a bot for a number with a loose word in it and it will quietly pick a meaning, then hand you a confident, wrong answer. This tip shows how one word like "got" or "orders" can mean several populations, and the one…
- [Lesson 4: Know What the Bot Can Actually Reach](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/04-know-what-the-bot-can-actually-reach/index.md): A bot's usefulness is bounded by what it's connected to, and it almost never tells you where that boundary is. Five generic examples show how a missing link, an unread thread reply or a doc it can't write turns into…
- [Lesson 5: Don't Trust "I Can't"](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/05-dont-trust-i-cant/index.md): A bot's "I can't" is often a prediction, not a test. It hasn't tried, or it guessed at your role. This tip shows how to tell a soft refusal from a real limit, so you push on the right ones and never around a genuine…
- [Lesson 6: Teach It Once](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/06-teach-it-once/index.md): Knowledge is what a bot has picked up. Skills are jobs you've written down for it. This tip shows how to save what a bot works out so nobody repeats it, why a good skill is mostly guardrails, and how saved rules can…
- [Lesson 7: The Second Message](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/07-the-second-message/index.md): Most people read the first answer and stop. Either they settle for it or give up on the tool. One follow-up line in the same chat usually turns a generic draft into a usable one, and asking the A.I. to interview you…
- [Lesson 8: Stop Re-Explaining Yourself](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/08-stop-re-explaining-yourself/index.md): If every Claude chat starts with you re-explaining your job and re-attaching the same file, a Project fixes it: shared knowledge and instructions in one place. This tip covers what sharing a project hands over (and…
- [Lesson 9: Claude Code Isn't Just for Developers](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/09-claude-code-isnt-just-for-developers/index.md): Claude Code's name keeps most non-developers away, but it works on any folder of ordinary files, driven by plain-English requests. This tip shows what it can do with screenshots, invoices and transcripts, what "it's…
- [Lesson 10: The Label Is Not the Definition](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/10-the-label-is-not-the-definition/index.md): The most common mistake in six weeks of bots' self-written lessons: trusting what a field is called instead of what it counts. A number with the wrong definition still ties out and reconciles, so nothing looks wrong…
- [Lesson 11: Your Bot in the Meeting](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/11-your-bot-in-the-meeting/index.md): A notetaker records one call and summarises it. A bot that's connected to your team's work can answer questions live, turn action items into real tickets, and remember what was decided last week. This tip shows how…
- [Lesson 12: Brief the Next Chat](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/12-brief-the-next-chat/index.md): Long chats drift without warning: early decisions count for less and can fall out of view. When a chat gets long, have it write a handoff and carry on in a fresh chat.
- [Lesson 13: Open the Source](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/13-open-the-source/index.md): AI-supplied citations can be perfectly formatted and completely invented, and pushed on a dead link a model may insist the page changed. A reference you haven't opened is a claim, not a source.
- [Lesson 14: Ask It to Disagree](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/14-ask-it-to-disagree/index.md): Models lean toward the view already in your question, so a yes to a leading question isn't a second opinion. Ask for the case against before you ask for advice: a review, not a fight.
- [Lesson 15: Treat Memory Like Notes](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/15-treat-memory-like-notes/index.md): AI memory is a small set of saved notes, not a mind. Notes can be never saved, saved wrong, off-topic or stale, and they won't keep up unless you update them.
- [Lesson 16: Don't Fire and Forget](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/16-dont-fire-and-forget/index.md): Agents act on real systems, and a rule typed into a prompt is not a lock. Put the lock in access and approval settings, and keep the judgment for steps you can't undo.

## Software Engineering 101

- [Series index](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/index.md): How to think about building software now that AI agents do much of the building. Each lesson centers on one practical rule: the loop that makes one piece of work correct.

- [Lesson 1: Plan, Build, Verify (and When to Skip It)](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/01-plan-build-verify/index.md): How do you fix code you don't understand when you only get one shot? Split the work into four roles: a person who owns the problem, a planner, a builder, and a verifier on a different model that can only read and…
- [Lesson 2: Rigor Follows Risk](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/02-rigor-follows-risk/index.md): A patch in ten minutes or the root cause in two days? Redeploy speed is only half the question: a redeploy fixes the code, but it doesn't undo what the code did. Product shape is uncertain and easy to change, so ship…
- [Lesson 3: Principles Over Languages](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/03-principles-over-languages/index.md): Why a computer science education built on ideas, not languages, still pays off, and why it matters more now that agents write the syntax.
- [Lesson 4: The Abstraction Ladder](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/04-abstraction-ladder/index.md): AI coding is one more rung on a ladder that runs from logic gates up. Stay at the top, and know when to send your agent down a rung.
- [Lesson 5: Understand Before You Change](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/05-understand-before-you-change/index.md): A perfect fix for the wrong problem is still wrong. Own the problem, restate it, reproduce and trace it, then fix the cause.
- [Lesson 6: Say What, Not How](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/06-say-what-not-how/index.md): Like a database optimizer, an agent does its best work when you state the outcome and the limits, not the steps. Too tight and too loose both cost you.
- [Lesson 7: Old Patterns, New Clothes](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/07-old-patterns-new-clothes/index.md): Pair programming, test-first and code review still work with agents in the seats. Cheaper tests change the trade, and three anti-patterns to watch for.
- [Lesson 8: Agile at Agent Speed](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/08-agile-at-agent-speed/index.md): Keep every scrum ceremony, but run the loop daily. Deploy continuously, ship features switched off behind a flag, and write down what you learned.
- [Lesson 9: Know What It Costs](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/09-know-what-it-costs/index.md): AI usage is the new currency of software. See the spend, the limit and a priced forecast before you start, and remember that owning software costs more than building it.
- [Lesson 10: Strict About Data, Relaxed About the Perimeter](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/10-strict-about-data/index.md): Be uncompromising about customer personal data and card data, pragmatic about where internal apps live, and see the whole series on one screen.

## Software Engineering 201

- [Series index](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/index.md): From Loop to Enterprise Systems: 101 gets one piece of work right with an AI loop. 201 is about whole systems: how building them changed across four eras, how to build them AI-native now, and the climb to agents that operate enterprise systems with governance, permissions, and an audit trail, ending with a capstone that builds one feature end to end.

- [Lesson 1: Four Eras of Building Systems](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/01-four-eras-of-building-systems/index.md): How we build big systems has changed from thirty, twenty and ten years ago to now, with agents doing much of the building. One useful lens is that architecture bends around whatever is scarcest. Machines were scarce…
- [Lesson 2: Build the Whole System, AI-Native](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/02-build-the-whole-system-ai-native/index.md): After the four eras, the first step from one loop to enterprise systems: what changes when you build a whole app or system with AI instead of one fix. A system is AI-native when agents and people can both read it,…
- [Lesson 3: Decompose the System into a Graph](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/03-decompose-the-system-into-a-graph/index.md): An enterprise system is too big for one loop, so draw it as a graph. A numbered plan only shows the order someone wrote the steps in; the test for any two steps is what crosses between them, and “and then” is not a…
- [Lesson 4: Parallel Agents, One Integration](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/04-parallel-agents-one-integration/index.md): Three agents can each pass their own check while the system is still broken, because no check has seen the parts together. Parallel work is only fast if it comes back together cleanly, so plan the integration first:…
- [Lesson 5: Governance: Where People Decide](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/05-governance-where-people-decide/index.md): Every era had a place where a person said yes: a change board signing off a whole release, then a teammate reviewing the code, then an approval on a pull request. Each was sized for people writing the code, so when…
- [Lesson 6: Quality, Feedback, and Observability](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/06-quality-feedback-and-observability/index.md): A green build says the code did what its tests asked; it says nothing about what happened last night. Ten years ago the scarce thing was seeing the whole system, and logs, metrics and traces answered "what…
- [Lesson 7: Skills as Building Blocks](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/07-skills-as-building-blocks/index.md): Three capable agents can do the same job three different ways when nobody wrote down how. Software has had several units of reuse: libraries, frameworks, then services behind an API. A skill reuses something…
- [Lesson 8: Routines, Pipelines, and Integration](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/08-routines-pipelines-and-integration/index.md): A job charges a card, the answer is lost, and the job tries again: unless someone designed that retry to be safe, the customer can be charged twice. Connecting systems is the oldest problem in this series, from…
- [Lesson 9: Agents That Operate Enterprise Systems](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/09-agents-that-operate-enterprise-systems/index.md) (outline): Agents that run the system, not just build it, with identity, least access, and an audit trail. The last step on the path: agents that operate enterprise systems day to day. Give each agent a clear job, its own…
- [Lesson 10: Capstone: One Feature, End to End](https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/10-capstone-one-feature-end-to-end/index.md): The capstone builds one small feature of a made-up subscription-billing system end to end, using every lesson in the series in order: a customer on a $30 monthly plan switches to a $300 annual plan ten days into the…

## Book

- [Silicon Valley C Players (preview)](https://clarkhuang.github.io/book/index.md): a free OpenBook (audiobook and videobook preview), coming in 2027. An embellished fictional dramatization; the narrator is Charlie Hack; the how-to-work-with-AI half is nonfiction. Written and interviewed by AI.
- [Preview transcript](https://clarkhuang.github.io/book-source/preview/transcript.md): full spoken text, with timestamps
- [Preview captions](https://clarkhuang.github.io/videos/book-preview.vtt): WebVTT for the videobook
- [Preview chapters](https://clarkhuang.github.io/videos/book-preview-chapters.json): chapter titles and start times
- [Preview scene scripts](https://clarkhuang.github.io/book-source/preview/scenes/): one markdown file per scene
- [Cover brief](https://clarkhuang.github.io/book-source/cover/PROMPT.md): how to describe or rebuild the cover
- [How this book is edited](https://clarkhuang.github.io/book/editorial-policy/index.md): editorial policy — conflicting recollections, how claims and sources are tracked, and a per-edition changelog of changed claims and sources

## Also on this site

- [Contribute with your AI](https://clarkhuang.github.io/contribute/index.md): A copy-paste prompt, GitHub issue forms, and a Connect your AI (MCP) section.
- [Copy this for yourself](https://clarkhuang.github.io/copy-this/index.md): How to fork or use this site as a template for your own OpenBook or learning series.
- [Ask the Book](https://clarkhuang.github.io/ask/index.md): In-browser search of lessons, chapters, scenes, and transcripts, plus a prompt you can send to your own AI.
- [Contributor credits](https://clarkhuang.github.io/credits/index.md): People who have contributed, listed by GitHub handle.
- [search-index.json](https://clarkhuang.github.io/search-index.json): Local search index used by Ask the Book.
